routes.label: Square and use the root sum

question: The sum of the real values of \(x\) satisfying \(\lvert x+2\rvert=2\lvert x-2\rvert\) is:
solution:
Because \(2\) is positive, \(2|x-2|=|2(x-2)|\). Two real numbers have the same absolute value exactly when they are equal or are opposites. Thus the original equation is equivalent to the following two possibilities:
\[
x+2=2(x-2)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=6,
\]
or
\[
x+2=-2(x-2)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=\frac23.
\]
The equal-or-opposite rule includes zero and covers every real possibility. Each branch also implies the original equality, so both solutions are valid and there are no others. Their sum is
\[
6+\frac23=\frac{20}{3}=6\tfrac23,
\]
choice E.
